summary.text: A group of vectors is linearly independent when none of them equals a linear combination of the others.
Equivalently, the only way to combine them into the zero vector 𝟎 is aᵢ = 0 for every coefficient.
Independence is part of the definition of a basis and is central to finding the dimension of a vector space.

facts.label: Dependence test
facts.value: One vector is zero or a combination of the others

facts.label: Single vector
facts.value: Dependent only if it is the zero vector

facts.label: Repeated vector
facts.value: Listing the same vector twice makes a sequence dependent

facts.label: Order
facts.value: Dependence does not depend on the order of the terms

facts.label: Locations
facts.value: n independent vectors are needed for n-dimensional space

items.prompt: A hiker is told: 3 miles north, 4 miles east, and also 5 miles northeast. How do these three directions relate as a group of vectors?

options.label: Independent, since they point different ways
Independent, since each has a different length
Dependent, since one is a combination of the others
Dependent, since two of them are perpendicular

items.explain: The northeast vector is a linear combination of the other two, so one of the three is unnecessary.

items.prompt: A list of arrows includes one arrow of length zero. Could the whole list be linearly independent?

options.label: No, a zero vector forces the list to be dependent
Yes, if the other arrows are independent
Yes, if the list is long enough
No, but only when the list has two arrows

items.explain: A collection containing the zero vector is necessarily linearly dependent.

items.prompt: You have a linearly independent list of arrows and you shuffle the order of the list. What happens to its independence?

options.label: It is lost whenever the first arrow moves
It is lost for lists longer than two
It depends on which arrow ends up last
It is unchanged by the reordering

items.explain: Linear dependence of a sequence does not depend on the order of its terms.

items.prompt: Two arrows point the same way, and one is twice as long as the other. Are they linearly independent?

options.label: Yes, because their lengths are different
No, because they are parallel
Yes, because there are only two
No, because both are nonzero

items.explain: Parallel vectors are dependent: one can be written as a multiple of the other.

items.prompt: Three arrows from one corner of a room all lie flat on the floor. Are they linearly independent?

options.label: Yes, since three arrows fill a room
Yes, since none of them is zero
No, since they all lie in one plane
No, since they start at the same point

items.explain: Three vectors in the same plane are dependent; independent ones in 3D must not share a common plane.

items.prompt: On a flat map, two independent directions locate any place. What is needed if altitude also matters?

options.label: A third independent vector
A longer second vector
A repeat of the first vector
Nothing more, since two always suffice

items.explain: If altitude is not ignored, a third vector must be added to the independent set; n independent vectors describe n-dimensional space.
